meta.name: Lotfollahi Lab Research Path — 24-Month Working-Professional Edition
meta.target: Computational biology researcher at Wellcome Sanger Institute (Lotfollahi Lab)
meta.background: Final-year / recently graduated computer engineering student with full-time job
design_notes: Original 12-month plan stretched to 24 months to accommodate job fatigue and weekday constraints
Peak deep-work sessions shifted to weekends; weekdays are lighter maintenance/reading tasks
Each phase is ~doubled in duration to reduce peak load — same total output, more sustainable pace
Buffer months (6, 12, 18) are recovery/catch-up months with no new hard deliverables
Outreach phases delayed to months where your portfolio is credibly dense

weekday_breakdown.monday: Theory — 30 min paper reading OR watching a lecture segment. No implementation. Low cognitive load.
weekday_breakdown.tuesday: Implementation micro-session — 1.5 hrs: debug previous weekend's code, fix one failing test, push a small commit.
weekday_breakdown.wednesday: Depth drill — pick ONE concept from the week and go deep: derive it, find analogues in other papers, write a 3-sentence note.
weekday_breakdown.thursday: Biology day (from month 8) — Scanpy/AnnData workflows, reading a Lotfollahi paper section, light planning. Skip before month 8.
weekday_breakdown.friday: Review + plan — 30 min: check what you were supposed to do this week, write 3 sentences in your research journal, plan Saturday deep work.

weekend_breakdown.saturday: Primary deep work: 3.5 hrs total. Morning block (2 hrs): major implementation or experiment. Afternoon block (1.5 hrs): analysis, visualization, commit and document.
weekend_breakdown.sunday: Secondary deep work: 3.5 hrs total. Morning (1.5 hrs): paper reading + annotations. Afternoon (1 hr): blog draft or README writing. Evening (1 hr): week review + planning next week's weekday micro-tasks.

recovery_rules: If a week goes bad (overtime, illness, burnout), skip ALL weekday tasks. Protect the weekend blocks.
If even one weekend day is lost, use the other to recover — do not try to compress two sessions into one.
Buffer months exist precisely for 2-4 week disruptions. Do not panic.
Never carry guilt across a buffer month boundary. Reset cleanly.

phases.name: Phase 1 — Core ML Foundations
phases.description: Build elite-level PyTorch, deep maths intuition, and GNN mastery. Spread over 10 months (vs 5 in the 12-month plan) to fit around job fatigue. Each weekend does what two weekdays used to do. Deliverables are identical — timeline is the only change. Non-negotiable base.

topics.name: PyTorch Deep Mastery
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read one PyTorch tutorial section. Wed: Trace one autograd computation by hand. Fri: Check what you implemented last weekend — does it make sense now?
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement one new PyTorch primitive from scratch. Sun: Write a 3-sentence explanation of what you built — rubber-duck style.
resources: PyTorch official tutorials (pytorch.org/tutorials)
Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai) — Chapters 1-5

topics.name: Backpropagation & Optimization
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read one Goodfellow section. Wed: Derive one update rule by hand — SGD first, then Adam. Fri: Review what confused you mid-week and note it.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement optimizer from scratch and verify outputs match PyTorch. Sun: Test different learning rates on a toy problem — visualize loss curves.
resources: Deep Learning — Goodfellow, Bengio, Courville (Chapters 6-8)
The Matrix Calculus You Need for Deep Learning — Parr & Howard (free PDF)

topics.name: Mathematics Foundations
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: One section of MML textbook — just read, no pressure to derive everything. Wed: Pick one concept (e.g. KL divergence) and derive it cleanly on paper.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement the concept in NumPy to verify intuition. Sun: Write a short 'explain it to a friend' note for your journal.
resources: Mathematics for Machine Learning — Deisenroth et al. (free PDF)
The Matrix Calculus You Need for Deep Learning — Parr & Howard

topics.name: Autoencoders
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read Goodfellow Chapter 14 section by section. Wed: Trace one forward pass through your autoencoder on paper.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Build encoder-decoder from scratch — no libraries. Sun: Visualize latent space with matplotlib, commit and document.
resources: Deep Learning — Goodfellow Chapter 14
Implement from scratch in PyTorch before using any library

topics.name: Variational Autoencoders
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Re-read one section of Kingma & Welling. Wed: Re-derive one component of ELBO from scratch — do this until it's muscle memory. Fri: Review your implementation notes from last weekend.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement one VAE component (encoder / reparameterization / decoder / ELBO loss) per weekend. Sun: Visualize outputs and write derivation notes for README.
resources: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes — Kingma & Welling 2013 (arXiv:1312.6114) — read 10 times
Tutorial on Variational Autoencoders — Doersch 2016 (arXiv:1606.05908)
Derive ELBO by hand before implementing

topics.name: Embeddings & Representations
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read one d2l.ai chapter section. Wed: Experiment with cosine similarity and embedding spaces on paper.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement Word2Vec skip-gram. Sun: Visualize embedding space with UMAP and write notes.
resources: d2l.ai Chapter 14-15
Word2Vec original papers (Mikolov et al. 2013)

topics.name: Transformers & Attention
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read one section of 'Attention Is All You Need.' Wed: Trace one multi-head attention computation by hand for a toy sequence length.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement scaled dot-product attention and multi-head wrapper from scratch. Sun: Run on a small toy task and visualize attention weights.
resources: Attention Is All You Need — Vaswani et al. 2017 (arXiv:1706.03762)
The Illustrated Transformer — Jay Alammar blog post
Annotated Transformer — Harvard NLP

topics.name: Graph Convolutional Networks
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Watch one CS224W lecture segment. Wed: Derive the GCN propagation rule by hand for a small 3-node graph.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement GCN from the adjacency matrix up — no PyG yet. Sun: Run Cora node classification, log results with wandb.
resources: Semi-Supervised Classification with GCN — Kipf & Welling 2017 (arXiv:1609.02907)
CS224W Lectures 1-8 — Stanford (YouTube, free)
Implement from scratch before using PyG

topics.name: Graph Attention Networks
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read GAT paper section. Wed: Trace the attention coefficient calculation by hand for one node.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement GAT from scratch — single head first, then multi-head. Sun: Visualize attention weights across neighbors.
resources: Graph Attention Networks — Veličković et al. 2018 (arXiv:1710.10903)
CS224W Lectures 9-12

topics.name: GraphSAGE
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read Hamilton et al. paper. Wed: Sketch the neighborhood sampling process for a large graph.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement GraphSAGE with mean aggregation. Sun: Test on inductive setting — held-out nodes not seen during training.
resources: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs — Hamilton et al. 2017 (arXiv:1706.02216)

topics.name: Message Passing Neural Networks
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read Gilmer et al. paper. Wed: Map GCN and GAT into the MPNN framework on paper.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement MPNN for QM9 molecular property prediction. Sun: Benchmark result against baseline, document.
resources: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry — Gilmer et al. 2017 (arXiv:1704.01212)

topics.name: Convolutional Neural Networks
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read Goodfellow Chapter 9 section. Wed: Derive the convolution operation by hand for a small kernel.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement a ResNet block from scratch. Sun: Train on CIFAR-10 — log accuracy curves.
resources: Deep Learning — Goodfellow Chapter 9
CS231n — Stanford (notes, free online)

topics.name: Graph Transformers
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read Graphormer / GPS paper. Wed: Compare graph attention mechanism to vanilla transformer attention on paper.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement positional encoding scheme for graphs. Sun: Compare with GCN baseline on same benchmark.
resources: Do Transformers Really Perform Bad for Graph Representation? — Ying et al. 2021
Recipe for a General, Powerful, Scalable Graph Transformer — Rampasek et al. 2022

topics.name: Geometric Deep Learning
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read one section of Bronstein et al. proto-book. Wed: Map one GNN architecture to the symmetry-group framework.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement one equivariant layer. Sun: Read selectively — this is a reference text, not a cover-to-cover read.
resources: Geometric Deep Learning: Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges — Bronstein et al. 2021 (free PDF)

deliverables: MLP trained on CIFAR-10 achieving 80%+ accuracy
Autoencoder repo with MNIST latent space visualization
VAE from scratch — full repo with ELBO derivation in README
GNN from scratch repo — GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, graph AE
GitHub commit history showing steady progression

projects.name: VAE From Scratch
projects.description: Implement a complete VAE with training, visualization of latent space, and generation. Do NOT use high-level libraries — build encoder, reparameterization, decoder, ELBO loss from primitive PyTorch. With a job, spread implementation across 4 weekends minimum.

milestones.description: Basic autoencoder working on MNIST
Add variational inference: KL divergence term + reparameterization trick
Train on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, log loss curves with wandb
Latent space visualization (PCA + UMAP) and latent interpolation
Conditional VAE: condition on class labels, generate class-specific samples
README with mathematical derivation of ELBO written from scratch

projects.name: Graph Neural Networks From Scratch
projects.description: Complete GNN implementations with mathematical derivations and experiments. Implement each architecture manually before switching to PyG. Spread across months 7-10 — one architecture per 2-3 weekends. Final repo should be a reference-quality resource.

milestones.description: GCN implementation + Cora node classification experiment
GAT implementation + attention visualization
GraphSAGE implementation + inductive experiment
Molecular property prediction on QM9 with MPNN
Graph autoencoder for link prediction
Clean README with math derivations, benchmark table, and learning notes

phases.name: Phase 2 — Enter Computational Biology
phases.description: Overlap with Phase 1 from month 8. Domain transition into single-cell computational biology. Learn biology through the computational lens. Weekday Thursday slot is reserved for biology from month 8 onward. With a job, this phase takes longer — that is expected and fine.

topics.name: Cell Biology for ML
topics.weekday_approach: Thu: Read one section of sc-best-practices.org. Keep biology reading separate from ML implementation days.
topics.weekend_approach: Sun: Watch one Theis lab lecture on YouTube. Write a 3-sentence summary connecting the biology to the ML problem.
resources: Single-cell best practices book — sc-best-practices.org (Chapters 1-3, free online)
A primer on single-cell RNA sequencing — YouTube lectures by Fabian Theis lab

topics.name: Scanpy & AnnData
topics.weekday_approach: Thu: Work through one Scanpy tutorial step. Fri: Write one observation about the data structure in your journal.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Complete one end-to-end Scanpy analysis step (normalization, HVG selection, PCA). Sun: Visualize the output and write annotations.
subtopics: AnnData structure: obs, var, obsm, uns
resources: Scanpy PBMC tutorial (scanpy.readthedocs.io)
Scanpy paper — Wolf et al. Genome Biology 2018
AnnData documentation and tutorials

topics.name: Batch Correction Methods
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read Luecken et al. benchmarking paper section. Thu: Run a harmony or scanorama tutorial on a public dataset.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement batch correction pipeline and evaluate with LISI/ASW metrics. Sun: Compare methods visually with UMAP.
resources: Benchmarking atlas-level data integration — Luecken et al. 2022
scvi-tools documentation

topics.name: Lotfollahi Papers Deep Dive
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Re-read one section of current Lotfollahi paper with annotations. Wed: Map one design decision from the paper to a specific PyTorch component you could implement.
topics.weekend_approach: Sun: Read one full Lotfollahi paper per fortnight — read it 2-3 times across two Sundays. Write detailed notes on architecture choices.
subtopics: trVAE — conditional generation with MMD loss
resources: scGen — Lotfollahi et al. Nature Methods 2019
trVAE — Lotfollahi et al. Bioinformatics 2020 (arXiv:1910.01791)
CPA — Lotfollahi et al. Nature Genetics 2023
expiMap — Lotfollahi et al. Nature Cell Biology 2023
chemCPA — Hetzel et al. 2022 (arXiv:2204.13545)

topics.name: Single-Cell ML
topics.weekday_approach: Thu: Read one scVI or foundation model paper section. Mon: Watch one lecture from a single-cell ML course.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Run scVI on a public dataset. Sun: Compare scVI latent space to PCA and note the differences in your journal.
resources: scVI — Lopez et al. Nature Methods 2018
Geneformer — Theodoris et al. Nature 2023
scGPT — Cui et al. Nature Methods 2024
Single-cell best practices book (Chapters 4-8)

deliverables: Scanpy PBMC tutorial completed end-to-end with own annotations
scGen reproduction with comparison to paper figures
trVAE reproduction with MMD loss implemented
CPA deep dive writeup — architecture explained in own words
Single-cell VAE for perturbation prediction — original project

projects.name: scGen Reproduction
projects.description: Reproduce scGen paper results from scratch. Implement the VAE architecture independently — do not copy lab code. With a job, give this 6-8 weekends. Document every discrepancy between your results and the paper. This is the single most important credibility signal for the lab.

milestones.description: Read paper 3 times — annotate every equation and design choice
Process Kang et al. 2018 IFN-β dataset with Scanpy
Implement VAE encoder, decoder, perturbation vector arithmetic
Train and evaluate: compare predicted vs actual stimulated cells
Write up results: what matched, what did not, and why
Publish GitHub repo with reproduction report

projects.name: trVAE Reproduction
projects.description: Reproduce trVAE — conditional generation across conditions using MMD loss. Focus on understanding the conditional architecture and the Maximum Mean Discrepancy regularization. Give this 4-6 weekends.

milestones.description: Understand MMD loss: derive it, implement it from scratch
Implement conditional encoder with condition embedding
Train on dataset from paper, evaluate conditional generation
Publish repo with clean README

projects.name: Single-cell VAE for Perturbation Prediction
projects.description: Build an original perturbation prediction system combining ideas from scGen and CPA. Make at least one architectural decision of your own. Train on Replogle et al. 2022 Perturb-seq. Benchmark against scGen and CPA baselines. Treat the write-up as a mini-paper. Allow 3-4 months of weekends.

milestones.description: Design architecture — document every choice and rationale
Implement conditional perturbation encoding with new design element
Train on Replogle et al. 2022 Perturb-seq dataset
Benchmark against scGen and CPA baselines quantitatively
GitHub repo with documentation, demo notebook, and results table

phases.name: Phase 3 — Become Publicly Visible
phases.description: Build research identity in parallel with all other work. With a job, writing output is lower volume — 6 blog posts over 15 months (one every ~10 weeks) is realistic and still impressive. Associate yourself with ML for biology, generative modeling, GNNs, perturbation learning. You need to be findable before you reach out.

topics.name: Technical Blog Writing
topics.weekday_approach: Fri: Write 2-3 sentences toward the current blog draft — do NOT try to write a full post on a weekday.
topics.weekend_approach: Sun: 1 hour on current blog post — outline, draft a section, or finalize. Publish only when it's good, not on a deadline.

blogPlan.title: scGen explained — how VAEs predict perturbation responses
My scGen reproduction — what matched, what did not, and why
GNNs for single-cell biology — a practical guide
Breaking down a recent Lotfollahi lab preprint
Building a perturbation VAE from scratch — architecture decisions

topics.name: GitHub Portfolio
topics.weekday_approach: Tue: Push at least one small commit (even documentation) to keep the streak alive. Fri: Check if READMEs need updating.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat or Sun: After completing any major implementation, immediately write the README before moving on.
subtopics: README quality: motivation, architecture, results, usage

topics.name: Community Engagement
topics.weekday_approach: Fri: 10-minute Twitter/X pass — post one sentence update or like/comment on one relevant thread. Do not spend more than 10 minutes.
topics.weekend_approach: Sun: After finishing a milestone, post a short thread showing what you built. Include one image (loss curve, latent space, or UMAP). Tag relevant researchers only when you have something specific to say about their work.
subtopics: Twitter/X: weekly progress posts — even one sentence counts
Tag @M_Lotfollahi on technical posts — not asking, just showing work
Follow: Lotfollahi lab PhD students and postdocs
Follow: Fabian Theis lab, Satija lab, Regev lab
Engage with preprints: post short threads breaking them down
File GitHub issues and PRs on scvi-tools and scanpy when you have something real to contribute

deliverables: 6 serious GitHub repos with clean documentation
Technical blog with 4-6 published posts
Visible research identity on Twitter/X
3 paper reproductions published
At least 1 open-source contribution merged

phases.name: Phase 4 — Direct Lab Alignment
phases.description: Targeted alignment with Lotfollahi lab ecosystem. Choose and execute one sharp specialization. Contribute to the open-source tools the lab builds on. This phase starts only after Phase 1 GNN work is done and Phase 2 reproductions are underway.

topics.name: Lab Ecosystem Study
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read one Lotfollahi lab paper per week during this focused mapping period. Thu: Map co-author connections — note who collaborates with whom.
topics.weekend_approach: Sun: Survey the lab GitHub repos — open issues, recent PRs, recent commits. Write a map of the ecosystem in a private Markdown file.
subtopics: all Lotfollahi lab publications and preprints
lab collaborators: Theis lab, Helmholtz Munich, Cambridge
PhD students and postdocs — read their papers too
lab GitHub repos: scgen, CPA, chemCPA
open issues and recent PRs in scvi-tools

topics.name: Specialization: Generative Models for Perturbation
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Read one section of the current specialization paper. Wed: Write one paragraph connecting the new method to what you already know.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Implement one component of the flow/diffusion model per weekend. Sun: Experiment and visualize — do not just read.
resources: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models — Ho et al. 2020
Flow Matching for Generative Modeling — Lipman et al. 2022
Causal machine learning for perturbation biology — Lotfollahi et al. perspectives

topics.name: Specialization: GNNs for Spatial Transcriptomics
topics.weekday_approach: Thu: Work through one Squidpy tutorial step. Mon: Read one spatial transcriptomics paper section.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Load a Visium or MERFISH dataset, build a tissue graph, run GNN on it. Sun: Visualize spatial domain results and note where the GNN helps vs hurts.
subtopics: spatial data formats: Visium, MERFISH, Xenium
tissue graph construction from spatial coordinates
resources: Squidpy documentation and tutorials
Spatially resolved transcriptomics — Staahl et al. 2016
STAGATE — Dong & Zhang 2022 (spatial domain identification with GNNs)

topics.name: Open Source Contributions
topics.weekday_approach: Tue: Find one good-first-issue in scvi-tools or scanpy. Read the codebase around it. Wed: Write a comment or draft a fix.
topics.weekend_approach: Sat: Work on the PR — implement fix, write tests, document. Do one PR per 4-6 weeks — quality over quantity.
subtopics: scanpy: documentation improvements, small bug fixes
Submit at least 2 PRs — aim for at least 1 merged
Write informative PR descriptions explaining the change
resources: scvi-tools GitHub — scverse/scvi-tools
scanpy GitHub — scverse/scanpy

deliverables: One clear specialization chosen and executed with a project
scvi-tools PR merged
Research-grade implementation of chosen specialization area
Full lab ecosystem mapped: papers, people, connections

phases.name: Phase 5 — Strategic Outreach
phases.description: Strategic outreach with substance. Become 'that engineering professional seriously transitioning into AI biology.' Never email Mo before you have scGen reproduction, VAE project, and visible GitHub. Reach PhD students and postdocs first. With a job, each outreach action is slower — that is fine because your output is what matters.

topics.name: Outreach Preparation
topics.weekday_approach: Fri: Check GitHub portfolio — would you be comfortable linking it to a researcher today? If no, what's missing?
topics.weekend_approach: Sun: Do one 'dry run' — write a draft outreach email, then delete it. Only send when the portfolio is ready.
subtopics: reproduce a paper before emailing its author
prepare specific technical question from reproduction
GitHub portfolio ready before first contact
Twitter/X presence established before first contact

topics.name: PhD Student / Postdoc Outreach
topics.weekday_approach: Research the target person's recent papers this week before sending the email.
topics.weekend_approach: Write and send one outreach email with scGen reproduction repo link and a specific technical question. Do not send more than 2 in the same week.
subtopics: email the PhD student whose paper you reproduced
include: reproduction repo link, one specific technical question
do not ask about internships or positions in first contact
follow up once after 3 weeks if no reply
topics.emailTemplate: Subject: Reproduction of [their paper] — question on [specific technical point]. Body: I reproduced [paper] and trained it on [dataset]. I found [specific observation]. I am trying to understand [specific question]. Link to repo: [GitHub link]. Would you be open to a brief async exchange? (~3 sentences max)

topics.name: Mo Lotfollahi Outreach
topics.weekday_approach: Draft the email on a weekday — iterate on it across 3 days before sending.
topics.weekend_approach: Final review and send on a weekend when you are not rushed. Email only after: scGen reproduction published, CPA studied, perturbation VAE project started.
subtopics: email only after: scGen reproduction, CPA study, perturbation VAE project started
link to GitHub — not a CV attachment
state one specific research question you want to explore
ask for collaboration or small project — not a position
one follow-up after 3 weeks if no reply
topics.emailTemplate: Subject: Implementation of CPA + proposed extension for [specific thing]. Body (150 words max): I am a CE graduate working full-time who reproduced scGen and studied CPA in detail. I built [perturbation VAE project name] — [one sentence on what it does]. GitHub: [link]. I noticed [specific technical observation from your reproduction]. I am curious whether [specific research question]. Is there room for a remote collaboration or small project? I can commit [X hours per week].

topics.name: Remote Research Collaboration & Applications
topics.weekday_approach: Mon: Research one program or opening. Fri: Add it to your application tracker.
topics.weekend_approach: Sun: Work on one application or statement per month. Do not rush these — quality matters enormously.
subtopics: PhD program applications: Cambridge, ETH Zurich, EMBL

deliverables: Outreach to 2-3 lab PhD students with reproduction repo links
Email to Mo Lotfollahi with substance — GitHub link, specific question
Formal applications to Sanger / Open Targets / EMBL-EBI programs
Research collaboration or engineer opportunity secured

anti_patterns: Do not try to compress two weekend sessions into one — you will burn out
Do not email Mo Lotfollahi before month 16 unless you have exceptional published output
Do not say 'I am very interested in your research' — every email says this
Do not ask for a PhD position — ask for a collaboration or small defined project
Do not send a CV attachment in the first email — link your GitHub instead
Do not start CPA implementation before finishing scGen reproduction
Do not use scGen lab code to reproduce scGen — implement from the paper
Do not disappear from Twitter/X between milestone completions — even one sentence per week counts
Do not learn Scanpy before having PyTorch and VAE foundations solid
Do not copy-paste implementations — type every line and understand every parameter
Do not skip buffer months — they exist precisely for when life gets in the way
Do not compare your pace to the 12-month plan — you have a job. The output is the same; the timeline is different.
Do not try to do weekday deep work after a mentally exhausting day at work — reading or journaling only
